Build a Sparse Coordinate-to-Feature Map

Source: R/design_mfa_maps.R
coordinate_feature_map.Rd

Constructs a sparse operator that maps a field on named reference coordinates into a subject's observed coordinate space. Each subject row is connected only to its `k` nearest reference coordinates, found with a k-d tree rather than an all-pairs distance matrix.

Usage

coordinate_feature_map(
  reference_coords,
  subject_coords,
  k = 4L,
  bandwidth = NULL,
  max_distance = Inf,
  kernel = c("gaussian", "inverse_distance", "nearest"),
  normalize_rows = TRUE,
  reference_names = NULL,
  subject_names = NULL
)

Arguments

reference_coords

Numeric reference-feature-by-coordinate matrix.

subject_coords

Numeric subject-feature-by-coordinate matrix.

k

Number of nearest reference coordinates retained per subject feature. Values larger than the number of reference features are truncated.

bandwidth

Positive Gaussian bandwidth. When `NULL`, the median positive retained-neighbor distance is used.

max_distance

Maximum permitted coordinate distance. Subject features with no retained neighbor inside this radius are rejected.

kernel

`"gaussian"`, `"inverse_distance"`, or `"nearest"`.

normalize_rows

Normalize each subject row to sum to one.

reference_names

Optional reference feature names; otherwise row names or deterministic generated names are used.

subject_names

Optional subject feature names; otherwise row names or deterministic generated names are used.

Value

A sparse subject-feature-by-reference-feature matrix.

Details

The returned matrix has subject features in rows and reference features in columns, matching the `feature_map` contract of [design_mfa()]. Gaussian and inverse-distance kernels are row-normalized by default. The construction is invariant to applying the same translation or orthogonal transformation to both coordinate sets.

Coordinates may be MNI voxels, surface coordinates, or another common Euclidean system. This function does not estimate anatomical registration; any transform into a common coordinate system must be applied beforehand.

Examples

reference <- cbind(x = 0:3, y = c(0, 0, 1, 1), z = 0)
rownames(reference) <- paste0("r", 1:4)
subject <- reference + 0.05
rownames(subject) <- paste0("s", 1:4)
coordinate_feature_map(reference, subject, k = 2, bandwidth = 0.2)
#> 4 x 4 sparse Matrix of class "dgCMatrix"
#>              r1           r2           r3           r4
#> s1 9.999870e-01 1.300713e-05 .            .           
#> s2 1.067703e-06 9.999989e-01 .            .           
#> s3 .            .            9.999870e-01 1.300713e-05
#> s4 .            .            1.067703e-06 9.999989e-01
